> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **12** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12aad143f717e140cc1ec7227281009ef37bb192` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `94bd0910b5a88e4e2a623cc700f347d0121feada` — the merge of head `088613bebab0047841f35dda237422bbe53942bf` into base `12aad143f717e140cc1ec7227281009ef37bb192`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 94bd0910b5a88e4e2a623cc700f347d0121feada && git checkout 94bd0910b5a88e4e2a623cc700f347d0121feada
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 12aad143f717e140cc1ec7227281009ef37bb192 088613bebab0047841f35dda237422bbe53942bf && git checkout -B drift-repro 12aad143f717e140cc1ec7227281009ef37bb192 && git merge --no-ff 088613bebab0047841f35dda237422bbe53942bf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 12aad143f717e140cc1ec7227281009ef37bb192
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 12aad143f717e140cc1ec7227281009ef37bb192` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The rest of the diff (generated `api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `declaration-map/`, `json-schema.manifest/`, `content/docs/references/**`, the strictness-ledger counts, the three new test files and the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the changeset and the two authorable-surface shards are READ here to judge ② and are not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

Gate verdicts on the head (the check-runs, not re-run): 60 success or skipped; two red lanes, both this diff's doing:
- `Check Changeset` — red: `Metadata-protocol: none` and `@objectstack/spec: patch` while the diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` and `system.json` (`none-baseline-moved`). The gate prescribes `Metadata-protocol: added` and at least `minor`. Judged under ②.
- `TypeScript Type Check` → `Type Check · source gates` — red at `check:llms-txt`: `packages/spec/llms.txt` declares system 37 (tree 38), api 33 (tree 34), heading 213 (tree 215). The two new modules `system/push-config.zod.ts` and `api/push-delivery.zod.ts` are the delta and the PR does not touch `llms.txt`. Must-fix (M2 below).
- `Spec property liveness` green — read as absence, not classification: the ledger's denominator is the registered metadata kinds plus the unregistered-kind and spec-only overrides (`liveness/README.md`); `api.json` governs `ApiEndpointSchema`, and no ledger governs `RegisterDeviceRequest`, `PushDeliveryData` or `PushServiceConfig`. The planned-marker rule is judged by hand under ④ (M3).

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:
- `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema` gains optional `vendor` (`PushVendorSchema`), `appId`, `locale`; `token` / `platform` / `deviceId` / `name` unchanged, no `.default()`, bare alias isomorphic — **right** as a widening. One caveat the changeset words wrong: the object is non-strict, so a body carrying a stray `vendor: 'hms'` was STRIPPED and accepted before and is REFUSED now. No served route reads this schema at this head (the client re-exports the type only, `packages/client/src/index.ts`; the device methods were removed in #3612), so no sender exists — a widening in fact, but "nothing a client writes today is refused" is not the exact statement. Should-fix wording (S5).
- `RegisterDeviceResponseSchema`, `UnregisterDevice*`, the `*Preferences*` schemas and `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES` unchanged; the route-catalog pin (3 endpoints) green — **right** (ruling 2 on the card thread, ADR-0049: a route row with no handler is not registered; the rows ride #29068).
- New public schemas: `PushVendorSchema`, `PushRouteSchema`, `PushDeliveryDataSchema` (`api/`), `ApnsTransportConfigSchema`, `FcmTransportConfigSchema`, `PushServiceConfigSchema` (`system/`), exported through `api/index.ts` and `system/index.ts`; six `z.input` aliases, pin count 811 → 817 — **right** (no default, no transform in any of the six). `PushRouteSchema` and `PushVendorSchema` are exported without `lazySchema`; `dispatcher.zod.ts` and `plugin-rest-api.zod.ts` carry the same precedent and lint is green — right.
- `INotificationService` gains optional `registerDevice`, `unregisterDevice`, `invalidateDeviceToken` typed from `api/protocol.zod` — **right**; the send-only implementation stays complete (tested), and `contracts/automation-service.ts` already imports `FlowRegistration` from the same module, so the layering has precedent.
- `api/protocol.zod.ts` imports `PushVendorSchema` from `system/push-config.zod.ts` — **right** on precedent (`ServedTranslationDataSchema` from `system/translation.zod`). ADR-0012 §10 names `notification/device.zod.ts` as the home; no `packages/spec/src/notification/` exists on `main`, and `system/notification.zod.ts` is the live home of the channel enum, so `system/` is the right directory.
- The authorable-surface shards gain 14 keys (`api/PushDeliveryData:notificationId|route`, `api/RegisterDeviceRequest:appId|locale|vendor`, `system/ApnsTransportConfig:environment|keyId|keyRef|teamId|topic`, `system/FcmTransportConfig:projectId|serviceAccountRef`, `system/PushServiceConfig:apns|fcm`) — this IS a metadata-protocol `added` by the gate's own definition. **Wrong** as declared (`none`); see ②.
- The `PushDeliveryDataSchema` JSDoc's derivation claim (explicit `payload.url` / `payload.actionUrl`, else `/OBJECT/ID` from the emit's source, else none) — **right** against `messaging-service.ts#actionUrlFor` and the notify node's `source` forwarding (`notify-node.ts`, the explicit `actionUrl` wins). No `notify` key added — right, the card preferred derivation.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset — **right** for the diff (every change is additive; see the one wording caveat in ①).
- `Metadata-protocol: none` and `'@objectstack/spec': patch` — **wrong**. The authorable-surface baseline moved by 14 keys; AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 and the `Check Changeset` step (`pr-automation.yml`, "WHICH LEVEL") say a new authorable key is `added` and takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, and the gate refused this head on exactly that line (`none-baseline-moved`). The round-2 claim on the card already declares `Metadata-protocol: added`; the PR body and changeset have to say the same. The PR body's argument ("no authoring door reads these") is the planned-marker question (④ M3), not a reason to grade `none` — #28920 is the precedent: `clientSource` was unread at its head and still declared `added` / `minor` with the marker. **Must-fix M1**: `Metadata-protocol: added` on the PR body and in `.changeset/29067-push-device-registry-spec.md`, level `minor`.
- No ADR-0087 disposition owed: nothing an author can write is renamed, removed or changed in meaning. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and `open_questions` (the os-dev-report lists none; the out-of-scope finding on `DEFAULT_NOTIFICATION_ROUTES`' JSDoc goes to #29068 — accepted):
- Wanted 2 (route rows) deferred to #29068 — **answered**: ADR-0049 retired `handlerStatus: 'planned'`, the runtime conformance test reds a catalog POST row with no served case, and the round-2 claim rules the same. Accepted.
- Wanted 3 (`UserDeviceSchema`) declined in the PR body as "ruling 3" — **not accepted**: the card asks for it, and the first server consumer #29068 names "`sys_user_device` per #29067's `UserDeviceSchema`" with ⛔ no `packages/spec/**` hunk of its own, so at this head the stored shape can be written by nobody. The round-2 claim on the card already re-adds `packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts`. Must-fix M5 under ④.
- Wanted 4 asks for four members (register, unregister, **list for a user**, invalidate); three are shipped and the omission is not explained in the PR body. No consumer at this head needs the list member (#29068's routes are register/refresh and unregister), so **escalated** to the seat: add `listDevices?(userId)` or record the ruling that drops it. Should-fix S4.
- Wanted 6, "the `.p8` key by `credentialRef`" / "service-account JSON by `credentialRef`" — the diff names `keyRef` and `serviceAccountRef`. Judged under ④ M4.
- Wanted 7 (`NotificationChannelSchema` JSDoc) rides the server slice — **answered**; the JSDoc on `main` still says push has no delivery implementation, which is true at this head. Accepted; hand-off named (#29041).
- Cloud-side surface: none proposed, none filed — **answered**; the PR says so, and nothing in the config shape is hosted-only.
- Verification not measured locally (dispatch-gates battery, full spec test and typecheck, scoped lint, final merge) — CI answered it: the two reds above are the result the battery would have shown.

New public names — each needs the maintainer's approval before landing (escalated, not FAIL reasons):
- Schemas and types: `PushVendorSchema` / `PushVendor`, `PushRouteSchema` / `PushRoute`, `PushDeliveryDataSchema` / `PushDeliveryData`, `ApnsTransportConfigSchema` / `ApnsTransportConfig`, `FcmTransportConfigSchema` / `FcmTransportConfig`, `PushServiceConfigSchema` / `PushServiceConfig`.
- Keys: `RegisterDeviceRequest.vendor`, `.appId`, `.locale`; `PushDeliveryData.notificationId`, `.route`; `PushServiceConfig.apns`, `.fcm`; `ApnsTransportConfig.teamId`, `.keyId`, `.topic`, `.environment`, `.keyRef`; `FcmTransportConfig.projectId`, `.serviceAccountRef`.
- Values: `vendor` ∈ `apns` | `fcm`; `environment` ∈ `sandbox` | `production`.
- Interface members: `INotificationService.registerDevice`, `.unregisterDevice`, `.invalidateDeviceToken`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** — against ADR-0012 §6, #29068 (server) and #29042 (ui):
- Holds: the three members are optional; `vendor` is the closed `PushVendorSchema` (an unknown vendor is `invalid_value` at `vendor`, five cases tested, including `APNS` and the empty string); the owner is the session's user and never a body member; refresh-by-`deviceId` and server minting are stated in the describe.
- **M3 (must-fix, shared with the other two schema files)**: no key added by this PR is read by any consumer at this head (census: no reader of `PushDeliveryData*`, `PushServiceConfig*`, `PushVendor*` or the three members outside `packages/spec`; the client holds a type re-export only), and no describe carries the `[PLANNED — not enforced]` marker naming the card that will read it. The #28920 precedent (`connector-auth.zod.ts#clientSource`) is the shape: the marker opens the describe, names the reader and the slice that lands it, and the comment above it says what takes the marker off. Here: `vendor` / `appId` / `locale` are read by #29068; `PushDeliveryData*` and `PushServiceConfig*` by #29041. Where a liveness ledger governs the type, a `planned` row goes with it; none governs these three types, so the describe marker is the carrier (the ledger gate's green is not a classification). The JSDoc prose ("nothing reads this shape until the push channel plugin lands") is not the machine-read channel and is not on `vendor` / `appId` / `locale` at all.
- **S1 (should-fix)**: the required / optional split is inverted against the ui consumer. #29042's input is the shell's `getPushToken()` → `{ token, vendor }`; the request REQUIRES `platform` and makes `vendor` optional, so the Console has to derive `platform` from `vendor` with no stated mapping, while the contract states only the reverse. State the vendor → platform mapping (`apns` → `ios`, `fcm` → `android`) or let `platform` be absent when `vendor` is present.
- **S2 (should-fix)**: `platform: 'web'` with no `vendor` is left undefined ("web has no core vendor"). State the outcome at the contract: refused at the route, or accepted and never delivered.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/notification-service.ts`** — against ADR-0012 §6 / §12 and #29068:
- Holds: optional members, one live owner per token, `NOT_FOUND` (not a distinct forbidden) for another user's device, the invalidated row kept and disabled with its time, re-registration re-enables. The toy implementation in the test exercises all three signatures.
- **S3 (should-fix)**: ownership is stated per USER, not per device row. The same user re-registering the same token under a new `deviceId` (the server-minted id lost with the shell's storage; the shell exposes no stable device id) leaves two enabled rows for one phone and one token — a double push the contract permits. The toy registry already deletes every other row holding the token; say so in the contract: one row per token, the newest registration owns it, whoever the user is.
- S4: `listDevices?(userId)` (Wanted 4) absent — see ③.

**`packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts`** — against ADR-0012 §8 (`data` of the push body), #29041 ask 3 and #29042 acceptance:
- Holds. I tried to break `PushRouteSchema`: `//host`, `/\host`, `/` + tab or newline + `/host`, `javascript:`, a bare `apps/...`, the empty string are refused by the regex (`^\/(?![/\\])[^\s\\\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$`); `\s` in JS covers NBSP, U+2028/2029 and the other Unicode spaces; a percent-encoded `%2F` stays a path segment under any parser; `/..//host` normalizes to a path on the base origin (`new URL`, and `pushState` refuses a cross-origin result), so it cannot leave the server. The derivation (`actionUrlFor`) is read and matches the JSDoc; dropping, never failing, a route that does not pass is the right call for a delivery.
- M3 applies (reader #29041).

**`packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts`** — against ADR-0143 D3, ADR-0012 §4 / §6, card Wanted 6 and #29041:
- Holds on the security property: every block is `strictObject` from birth; an inline secret is refused by name under `key` / `privateKey` / `p8` / `authKey` / `signingKey` / `secret` (APNs) and `serviceAccount` / `serviceAccountJson` / `credentials` / `privateKey` / `secret` / `serverKey` (FCM), each with the reference key as the prescription (tested, `unrecognized_keys`, message names the ref key); a PEM block or a JSON document pasted into the reference is refused by `secretReference` (`^[^\s{}]+$`). The vendor enum is closed (`apns` | `fcm`, `.options` pinned), and `environment` is closed. Placement beside `email-config.zod.ts` matches the card's "where per-environment email transport selection lives"; not wiring it into the stack definition before a reader exists is the right ADR-0049 posture.
- **M4 (must-fix)**: the reference key is not the one D3 names. D3: "Every secret an author names is a `credentialRef`, resolved through `CredentialResolver`"; the card says the same twice. The diff names `keyRef` and `serviceAccountRef` and puts `credentialRef` in `aliases`, so an operator who writes the house spelling is REFUSED and sent to the new one. Each block holds exactly one secret, so `credentialRef` fits without ambiguity. Rename both to `credentialRef` (and move `keyRef` / `serviceAccountRef` to `aliases`), or carry the two new names to the maintainer with the reason D3 should not apply here; either way the record cannot pass a schema that refuses the ADR's own key.
- **S6 (should-fix)**: APNs certificate-auth spellings (`certificate`, `cert`, `p12`, `pem`) are refused as unknown keys with no prescription; one `guidance` line saying token auth is the only transport closes it.
- M3 applies (reader #29041, the push channel plugin).

**`packages/spec/src/api/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/index.ts`** — the two `export *` lines are right and match the generated `export-origins` / `api-surface` shards.
- **M2 (must-fix)**: the two new modules red `check:llms-txt` (`Type Check · source gates`): update `packages/spec/llms.txt` — system 37 → 38, api 33 → 34, heading 213 → 215 — and the `Key Schemas` prose of both rows (Push Config beside Email / SMS Config; Push Delivery under api), as the gate's header asks: the number and the row together.

**M5 (must-fix, the missing file)**: card Wanted 3 — a `UserDeviceSchema` per ADR-0012 §6 narrowed to what core ships (`vendor` from `PushVendorSchema`, `platform`, `token`, `deviceId`, `appId`, `locale`, `enabled`, `invalidated_at`, `last_seen_at`), stating (a) user-owned or user-and-organization-owned, (b) one live owner per token, (c) the invalidation fields — is absent, and its first consumer #29068 is ordered to build `sys_user_device` on it with no spec hunk of its own. The round-2 claim on the card already names `packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts`; land it here with the `[PLANNED — not enforced]` marker naming #29068.

Must-fix: M1 (declaration and level), M2 (`llms.txt`), M3 (planned markers), M4 (`credentialRef`), M5 (`UserDeviceSchema`). Should-fix: S1–S6. No security mechanism finding: the inline-secret and off-server-route refusals hold as built; M4 is a rule-level naming conformance.
